question: What specific capacity in mAh/g did the strained V2O5 films deliver?
rendered:
The document "Tunable Mechanochemistry of Lithium Battery Electrodes" is the one that likely contains the answer. 

According to page 5, the cyclic voltammograms of the unstrained and strained states of the surface V2O5 film at a scan rate of 30 mV/s were obtained. However, the specific capacity delivered by the strained V2O5 films is not explicitly mentioned. 

But on page 4, it is mentioned that the V2O5 (α phase) can intercalate lithium ions in the interlayer spacing along the ‘c’ direction. It also mentions that the V2O5 undergoes a series of electrochemically and structurally reversible transformations from the α phase to the ε phase and the δ phase during intercalation and deintercalation of Li^+ ions. 

However, on page 4, Figure 4a shows the cyclic voltammograms of the unstrained (0%) and strained (−0.35%, −0.5% based on ‘c’ direction) at a scan rate of 30 mV/s normalized to the maximum peak current. 

It is also mentioned on page 4 that for both ∼80 nm and ∼40 nm (see Supporting Information, Figure S14) V2O5 films, similar shifts in values of ΔEeq(avg) were observed (see Supporting Information, Figure S15) owing to the similar % “locked in” elastic strains. 

However, on page 5, it is mentioned that a change in intercalation energy of ∼75 meV (∼75 mV) was calculated with an applied in-plane strain of +1.5% on the V2O5 lattice (Figure 4d), comparable to the measured change in potential of ∼40 mV at about ∼1.66% in-plane prestrain in Figure 4b.
